# @ternent/seal

> Detached Ed25519 proofs over SHA-256 content hashes.

Three exports from the package root: `createSealHash`, `createSealProof`, `verifySealProof`.
Types: `SealProof`, `SealHash`, `SealVerification`. Declarations: `dist/index.d.ts`.

```ts
import { createIdentity } from "@ternent/identity";
import { createSealHash, createSealProof, verifySealProof } from "@ternent/seal";

const identity = await createIdentity();
const proof = await createSealProof({
  signer: identity, // any { publicIdentity, sign } from @ternent/identity
  subject: { hash: await createSealHash(bytes) },
});
const { valid } = await verifySealProof(proof, bytes);
if (!valid || proof.signer.id !== trustedPublisher.id) throw new Error("Untrusted");
```

- `verifySealProof` never throws; malformed proofs return `valid: false`.
- `signatureValid` and `hashMatch` are reported separately; `valid` needs both.
- Seal does not decide trust. Pin the expected signer yourself.
- Seal has no recipients or encryption. To prove encrypted data, seal its ciphertext bytes.
- To prove several files, seal a manifest of their hashes and check each file yourself.
